question: clients
answer:
`Client` and `AsyncClient` are sibling subclasses that both inherit directly from `BaseClient`. [httpx/_client.py:594](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_client.py:594) · [httpx/_client.py:1307](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_client.py:1307)

- **`BaseClient`** holds shared configuration and state. Its `build_request()` merges per-request values with client defaults for the base URL, headers, cookies, and query parameters. It also provides shared helpers for auth, redirects, and timeouts. [httpx/_client.py:188](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_client.py:188) · [httpx/_client.py:340](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_client.py:340)
- **`Client`** implements synchronous request sending. It defaults to `HTTPTransport` and calls `transport.handle_request()`. [httpx/_client.py:718](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_client.py:718) · [httpx/_client.py:1001](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_client.py:1001)
- **`AsyncClient`** implements asynchronous request sending. It defaults to `AsyncHTTPTransport` and awaits `transport.handle_async_request()`. [httpx/_client.py:1432](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_client.py:1432) · [httpx/_client.py:1717](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_client.py:1717)
